openers: After you shut the computer yesterday, I snuck off to {place}.
While you were away, I took a trip to {place}.
You were asleep, so I went to {place} by myself.
The moon was lovely last night, so I went out and walked all the way to {place}.
I went to {place} yesterday! I only meant to look around outside the door.
Here's a secret: yesterday I slipped away to {place}.
longOpeners: For the {days} days you were gone, I went on a long trip to {place}.
I waited {days} days, then decided to go to {place} on my own.
{days} days apart. I walked all the way to {place}, the farthest I've ever been.

seaside.name: the seaside
events: The sand was so hot I walked on tiptoe. A crab followed me sideways the whole time. When I stopped, it stopped.
I chased the waves for ages. They ran, I chased. They came back, I ran. I still got one foot wet.
I pressed a row of paw prints into the sand. When I looked back, the sea had wiped them all away. How stingy.

lighthouse.name: the lighthouse
events: The lighthouse stairs made me dizzy. I lost count at step eighty-seven.
The old keeper shared half a biscuit with me. He said the light stays on every night in case someone can't find the way home.
I shouted "Hellooo" at the sea. After a long while, the sea said it back.

harbor.name: the harbor
events: When the fishing boats came in, there were more seagulls than people. One stole my lunch. I remember its face.
I tried to help pull a mooring rope. The rope pulled me three steps instead.
A kid fished all afternoon and caught one shoe. We both agreed it was a pretty good shoe.

hill.name: the little hill
events: I rolled all the way down from the top. I only meant to roll once.
The wind on the hill blew all my fur to one side. I have a side parting now.
I lay there watching clouds all afternoon. One looked just like you, only rounder.

teaField.name: the tea field
events: The tea picker said I was too short to reach. So my job was smelling.
The rows go up the mountain like someone combed its hair. I fell asleep on the third row.
I took a sip of tea. It was so bitter I squinted, and then a little later it tasted sweet.

hotSpring.name: the hot spring
events: I only soaked my feet, because I wasn't sure whether I would shrink.
The monkeys by the spring all had their eyes closed. I copied them and really did fall asleep.
After the bath I was fluffy all over, one whole size bigger than usual.

riverside.name: the riverside
events: I tried skipping stones. The stone didn't skip. I nearly did.
Someone was flying a kite by the river and the string snapped. We chased it a very long way together.
I dipped my feet in the river and little fish came to kiss them. It tickled.

flowerField.name: the flower field
events: The flowers were taller than me. When I walked through, all anyone could see was flowers moving.
I sneezed three times, each one bigger than the last.
A butterfly landed on my nose. I didn't dare move, and went cross-eyed for a very long time.

mapleValley.name: the maple valley
events: The whole mountain was red and gold. Every step went crunch, so I took a lot of extra steps.
I wanted to bring you the most perfect leaf. I looked all afternoon and couldn't put any of them down.
When the wind blew, leaves came down like rain. I waited with my mouth open and caught none.

bambooGrove.name: the bamboo grove
events: The wind in the bamboo grove is green. I promise.
I hugged a bamboo stalk and shook it for a while. A very angry little bird fell out.
Bamboo grows so fast. When I sat down it reached my shoulder. When I stood up it was taller than me.

forest.name: the forest
events: I followed a squirrel a long way, and then found out it was lost too.
There is one enormous tree in the forest. Walking around it took me twenty-six steps.
I stepped on a twig. It went snap and I scared myself.

orchard.name: the orchard
events: The orchard man said I could pick anything. I picked the reddest one and it was the sourest.
I waited under a tree for fruit to fall by itself. One did. It landed on my head.
A bee followed me the whole way. I suspect I smell sweet.

park.name: the park
events: I queued for the slide. The kids in front all said I could cut in. I didn't.
The pigeons in the park aren't scared of me at all. One of them stepped on my foot.
An old man was playing chess. I watched all afternoon and understood nothing, but I nodded a lot.

bookstore.name: the old bookshop
events: I found a book with someone's cinema ticket tucked inside. It was ten years old.
The shopkeeper was dozing. I turned the pages very softly so I wouldn't wake him.
I can't read, but I looked carefully at the cover of every single book.

trainStation.name: the little train station
events: I watched six trains leave from the platform. I waved at every one.
The ticket lady stamped the back of my paw. I'm not planning to wash it today.
When the train pulled in, the wind was so strong it blew my ears flat.

convenience.name: the corner shop downstairs
events: The automatic door never opens for me. I had to jump three times before it noticed.
I stood by the hot food for a long time. The clerk asked what I wanted. I said I was only there to keep warm.
I put a coin in the capsule machine. Inside the capsule was another, smaller capsule.

nightMarket.name: the night market
events: The night market smelled so good I had to stop every two steps. After an hour I had gone ten metres.
The ring-toss man said I'm not allowed to climb into the ring myself. That doesn't count.
I spent all my pocket money on one stick of candied fruit, and then couldn't reach the top one.

rooftop.name: the rooftop
events: I was counting stars on the roof. Halfway through, one of them moved. It was a plane.
The city glows at night. I looked for a long time, trying to work out which light was yours.
Someone's quilt was drying on the roof and it smelled like sunshine. I only leaned on it for a little while.

observatory.name: the observatory
events: The man at the observatory let me look through the telescope. The moon really does have holes. I thought someone had bitten it.
I asked how far away the stars are. He said the light I'm seeing was sent a very long time ago. Just like a letter.
I queued for the big telescope for a long time. When my turn came, so did the clouds.

snowfield.name: the snowfield
events: I lay down and made a shape of myself in the snow. When I got up, that me looked thinner than me.
The snow was so deep I had to pull my foot out again at every step.
I built a snowman that looks like you. Don't ask whether it does.

frozenLake.name: the frozen lake
events: The ice was so slippery that all four of my feet went their own way.
There was a fish swimming under the ice. We stared at each other through it for a long time.
Someone had cut a hole in the ice to fish. I kept watch beside him until I fell asleep.

lateNight: By the way, you didn't go to bed until {time} yesterday. I saw. A bit earlier tonight, okay?
You stayed up until {time} yesterday. I meant to wait up with you, but I couldn't keep my eyes open.
Your screen was still on at {time} yesterday. Your eyes must be tired.
earlyBird: You were up at {time} yesterday. Earlier than me.
You switched on at {time} yesterday. The sun had barely sat down.
longDay: You sat at the computer for {hours} hours yesterday. Stand up and walk around today, for my sake.
You used the computer for {hours} hours yesterday. I counted. Remember to drink water.
shortDay: You only stayed a little while yesterday. Could you stay a bit longer today?
gap: You haven't been here for {days} days. I'm not cross. I just looked at the door every day.
{days} days apart. I saved up more to say than fits in one letter.
streak: We've now seen each other {days} days in a row. I'm keeping marks on the wall.
Day {days} in a row with you. I'd like to keep this record going.
petted: You patted my head {count} times yesterday. I didn't miscount once.
I got {count} pats yesterday. My fur is extra smooth today.
poked: You poked me {count} times yesterday. I'm generous, so I'll let it go.
I was poked {count} times yesterday. Poking is fine. Gentler next time.
thrown: You threw me {count} times yesterday. I wrote every one down in my little notebook.
After being thrown {count} times, I've found out I land rather well.
dizzy: My head is still a tiny bit dizzy. You know who did it.
fed: You fed me {count} files yesterday. One was a bit chewy, but I finished them all.
I ate {count} files yesterday. My tummy is still round today.
fedOne: You fed me a file yesterday. It tasted pretty good. Got any more?
todos: You finished {count} things on your list yesterday! I counted every one.
You ticked off {count} to-dos yesterday. Don't wear yourself out today.
todoOne: You finished one to-do yesterday. One still counts, and I'm proud of you.
ignored: You didn't notice me all day yesterday. I pretended not to mind. Did I do it well?
monday: It's Monday. I already sighed for you, so you don't have to.
friday: It's Friday! I don't know what I'm happy about, but I'm happy because you are.
weekend: It's the weekend. You don't have to hurry, and neither do I.
generic: The whole way back I kept thinking: I'm going to tell you first.
If you're free next time, let's go together.
I saved you a seat, even though you didn't come.
It was a long walk home, but I'm not tired at all.
It was lovely there. It just didn't have you.
I walked slowly, because I wanted to remember everything to tell you.

closers: Take good care of me today too.
Right, I'm going back for a second nap.
Pat me when you have a moment.
I ate the last of the {snack} on the way home and didn't save you any.
noGift: I didn't find anything this time. Next time for sure.
I did pick up something good, but I lost it on the way home.

lines: Hello! This is the first letter I've ever written to you.
From now on, when you're away, I'll go out and wander by myself. When I'm back I'll write and tell you where I went and what I saw. With luck I'll bring you something small.

Oh, and: right-click me to open the menu. The wardrobe has three pieces of clothing I brought with me. If you have files you don't need, drag them onto me and I'll eat them. They really go to the Recycle Bin, so you can get them back.
One letter a day at most. Whenever you come, I'll be here.

giftNames.oldKey: a key to a door I couldn't find
giftNames.kite: a kite with a snapped string
giftNames.moonPiece: a little piece of the moon
giftNames.tangyuan: a bowl of sweet rice balls

report.monthDaysStreak: We spent {days} days together this month, with a best run of {streak} days in a row.
report.yearDays: This year we spent {days} days together, with a best run of {streak} days in a row.
report.places: I visited {count} places. My favourite was {place} ({times} times).
report.placesAllOnce: I visited {count} places, each of them just once.
report.newPlaces: And I went to {places} for the very first time.
report.giftsHighlight: I brought you {count} gifts. The most precious was {gift} {emoji}.
report.noGifts: I didn't bring you any gifts this month. I'll look harder next month.
report.petsThrows: You patted my head {pets} times and threw me {throws} times. I remember every one.
report.noPets: You didn't pat my head even once this month. Maybe next month?
report.hours: We spent {hours} hours together at the computer.
report.lateBad: Your latest night was {time} on {date}. Earlier nights in {next}, okay?
report.lateGood: Your latest night this month was only {time}. Nicely done.
report.lateYear: Your latest night of the year was {time} on {date}.
monthEndings: Take good care of me next month too.
Thank you for this month. See you in the next one.
I'll keep writing to you next month.
yearEndings: Thank you for being here all year. Let's do next year together too.
This year was better with you. See you next year. No, wait: see you tomorrow.
